blocks.html: 1.1. If \(S\) is a scheme of characteristic \(p\), we denote by \(F_S\) the Frobenius endomorphism of \(S\) (given by the identity on the underlying topological space and \(a \mapsto a^p\) on \(\mathcal{O}_S\)). If \(u : X \to S\) is a morphism of schemes, with \(S\) of characteristic \(p\), one has a commutative diagram
\[ \xymatrix{ X \ar@/^2.2ex/[rrd]^{F_X} \ar@/_2.2ex/[rdd]_{u} \ar[rd]|{F_{X/S}} & & \\ & X' \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d]^{u} \\ & S \ar[r]_{F_S} & S } \]

where the square is cartesian; the morphism \(F_{X/S}\) is by definition the relative Frobenius morphism of \(X/S\). We will denote it simply by \(F\) when no confusion can result. For \(x\) a local section of \(\mathcal{O}_X\), with image \(x \otimes 1\) in \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\), one has \(F^*_{X/S}(x \otimes 1) = F^*_X(x) = x^p\). Example: if \(X\) is defined by equations \(f_\alpha = \sum a_{\alpha,m} T^m\) in the affine space \(S[T_1, \dots, T_n] = \mathbf{A}^n_S\), \(X'\) is defined by the equations \(f^\sigma_\alpha = \sum a^p_{\alpha,m} T^m\) in \(\mathbf{A}^n_S\), and \(F_{X/S}\) is given by \(T_i \mapsto T^p_i\).

Let \(\Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) be the de Rham complex of \(X/S\). We will systematically use relative de Rham complexes and, in what follows, will sometimes abbreviate \(\Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) to \(\Omega^{\bullet}_X\), or even \(\Omega^{\bullet}\). The complex \(F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) (where \(F = F_{X/S}\)) is a complex of \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\)-modules, with linear differential. If \(X\) is smooth over \(S\), the \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules \(\Omega^i_{X/S}\) are locally free of finite type (as are the \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\)-modules \(\Omega^i_{X'/S}\)), and the same holds for the \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\)-modules \(F_* \Omega^i_{X/S}\), since \(F\) is finite locally free (of rank \(p^r\) if \(X\) has relative dimension \(r\) over \(S\)). Moreover, one has the following fundamental result, due to Cartier [4]:

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 1.2 (Cartier)

Let \(X \to S\) be a smooth morphism, with \(S\) of characteristic \(p\). There exists a unique homomorphism of graded \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\)-algebras

\[ C^{-1} : \bigoplus_i \Omega^i_{X'/S} \to \bigoplus_i \mathscr{H}^i F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \]

such that \(C^{-1} d(x \otimes 1) = \) class of \(x^{p-1}\, dx\) for every local section \(x\) of \(\mathcal{O}_{X'}\), and \(C^{-1}\) is an isomorphism.
(The existence and uniqueness of \(C^{-1}\) are easy, and one checks that \(C^{-1}\) is an isomorphism by reduction to the case of the affine line, and a direct computation: cf. Katz [15, 7.2].)

1.3. If \(k\) is a perfect field of characteristic \(p\), we denote by \(W(k)\) the ring of Witt vectors of \(k\), and \(W_n(k) = W(k)/p^n\). The ring \(W_n(k)\) is flat over \(\mathbf{Z}/p^n\), equipped with an isomorphism \(W_n(k)/p W_n(k) \xrightarrow{\sim} k\), and is characterized up to unique isomorphism by these properties; one has \(W(k) = \varprojlim W_n(k)\). The Frobenius automorphism of \(k\) induces, by functoriality, an automorphism \(\sigma\) of \(W(k)\) (resp. \(W_n(k)\)), given by \(\sigma(a_0, a_1, \dots) = (a_0^p, a_1^p, \dots)\).

1.4. Let \(A\) be an abelian category. For \(n \in \mathbf{Z}\), the truncation \(\tau_{\leqslant n} L\) of a complex \(L\) of \(A\) is the subcomplex of \(L\) with components \(L^i\) for \(i<n\), \(\operatorname{Ker}(d)\) for \(i=n\), and 0 for \(i>n\). One has \(H^i \tau_{\leqslant n} L = H^i L\) (resp. 0) if \(i \leqslant n\) (resp. \(i>n\)). One sets \(\tau_{<n} L = \tau_{\leqslant n-1} L\). One defines dually \(\tau_{\geqslant n} L\), a quotient of \(L\), with \(H^i \tau_{\geqslant n} L = H^i L\) (resp. 0) if \(i \geqslant n\) (resp. \(i<n\)).

The shifted complex \(L[n]\) is the complex with components \(L[n]^i = L^{i+n}\) and differential \(d_{L[n]} = (-1)^n d_L\). For \(M\) an object of \(A\), we again denote by \(M\) the complex reduced to \(M\) placed in degree 0; \(M[n]\) is then the complex reduced to \(M\) placed in degree \(-n\).
1.5. If \(X\) is a scheme, we denote by \(D(X) := D(X, \mathcal{O}_X)\) the derived category of the category of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules.

1.6. Let \(\tilde S\) be a scheme and \(S\) a closed subscheme defined by an ideal of square zero. If \(X\) is a flat \(S\)-scheme, one says that \(X\) is liftable over \(\tilde S\) if \(X\) admits a lifting over \(\tilde S\), i.e. a flat \(\tilde S\)-scheme \(\tilde X\) equipped with an isomorphism \(\tilde X \times_{\tilde S} S \xrightarrow{\sim} X\); if \(X\) is smooth over \(S\), \(\tilde X\) is automatically smooth over \(\tilde S\).
